# Pharmacology: PK, PD and the drug rows

[All modules](README.md) · [Known misses](../validation/known-misses.md#pharmacology) · 20 source files, 2387 lines · 44 test files

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
The drug model computes, every 100 ms, the concentration of every drug given — boluses, infusions, target-controlled
infusions and volatile agents — in plasma and at its effect sites, and combines them into the effects the rest of the
engine reads: the circulation's drug multipliers, β-blockade, and the per-agent concentrations the neuro, organ and
breathing models use for depth, neuromuscular block and ventilatory depression. A clinician-educator reads it to see how
dose, patient covariates and drug interactions shape the response; an embedding developer reads it for the drug
library rows and the outputs other modules consume.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
- Drugs with a published model use linear mammillary compartment PK with one or more effect sites: three amount states
  exchange through rate constants derived from volumes and clearances, and each effect site follows the central
  concentration with its own ke0; the step is exact for a constant infusion rate and a bolus adds to the central
  compartment at once (tables §6.1; `l2/pk/compartment.ts`).
- The PK parameters are the published models' own, as functions of the patient, for example Eleveld 2018 for propofol
  with its arterial ke0 (tables §6.1; `l2/pk/models.ts`), with each model's own covariate formulas (tables §6;
  `l2/pk/covariates.ts`).
- Drugs without a PK model use a gamma effect curve E(t) = (t/tp)^n·e^{n(1 − t/tp)}, 1 at the peak time, scaled by
  dose over a reference dose and summed over doses into a normalised effect-site value (B §4.9, tables §6.1;
  `l2/pk/gamma.ts`).
- Volatile agents and N2O follow a breathing-circuit volume, the alveolar gas and three tissue groups (vessel-rich,
  muscle, fat) in parallel on the cardiac output, with uptake set by blood/gas solubility; the vessel-rich tension is
  the brain's (Eger; Mapleson; Miller ch. 18–19; `l2/pk/volatile.ts`).
- Effects use a sigmoid Emax relation, competitive antagonism raises the EC50 by (1 + Cant/Ki), and hypnotic–opioid
  interaction uses a Greco/Minto response surface U = Uh + Uo + α·Uh·Uo (Bouillon 2004; `l2/pk/pd.ts`).
- Hypnotic potency falls with age by the Eleveld term C50(age) = C50(35)·e^(−k(age − 35)) (tables §5d;
  `l2/pk/combine.ts`, `l2/pk/pd.ts`); catecholamine efficacy falls with acidaemia (tables §5b.1, §6.2;
  `l2/pk/pd.ts`).
- Volatile per-MAC effects on the circulation are linear in concentration, E = emax·c/ec50, clamped (tables §6.3;
  `l2/pk/row.ts`); propofol's circulatory effect uses E = Ce/(Ce + 3.5) on SVR, contractility, venous capacity and the
  reflex (tables §6.3, Cullen 1987; `l2/pk/data/rows-anaesthetic.ts`).
- Neuromuscular blockers have two effect sites, adductor pollicis and diaphragm/larynx, and the block is
  T1 = 1 − Ce^γ/(Ce^γ + EC50^γ) (Plaud 1995; tables §5d; `l2/pk/nmb.ts`).
- Target-controlled infusion picks one rate per interval: the rate that puts plasma concentration on target (Jacobs
  1990) or the largest rate whose predicted effect-site concentration never overshoots (Shafer & Gregg 1992)
  (`l2/pk/tci.ts`); the context-sensitive half-time follows Hughes, Glass & Jacobs 1992 (`l2/pk/csht.ts`).
- Hepatic, renal and temperature factors scale each drug's clearance (research/13; `l2/pk/pipeline.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

| `HEMO_SYN_MAX` | `0.2` | — | Billard 1994; research/14; [ENG sizes; fit target [P] | An opioid on board deepens a HYPNOTIC's vasodilation and venodilation beyond the independent product — the hypnotic class's `svr` and `v0Frac` effects × (1 + HEMO_SYN_MAX·u/(u + HEMO_SYN_U50)), u = `uOpioid`. [ENG sizes; fit target [P]: Billard 1994 Anesthesiology 81:1384 (n = 120, ASA 1–2), propofol 2–3.5 mg/kg, systolic fall 28 mmHg alone vs 53 mmHg after fentanyl 2 µg/kg 5 min earlier (ratio 1.9) and 50 mmHg after 4 µg/kg — the same within the study, hence the saturating form (fentanyl 2 µg/kg is u ≈ 3.5 at 5 min, 4 µg/kg ≈ 7).] Hypnotic class only: midazolam co-induction is additive for pressure (research/14). SIZE: 0.2 is the LARGEST that keeps the two sourced bands this interaction feeds back into through the flow-dependent distribution — the induction apnoea (fentanyl pair 60–240 s: 108 s at 0.2, 513 s at 2) and the laryngoscopy-response blunting ratio (0.2–0.7: 0.22 at 0.2, 0.19 at 0.6). It reaches a Billard ratio of 1.16 against the paper's 1.9 — a known miss. |
